subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Availability Heuristic
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Availability Heuristic.

hook.text: After a plane crash on the news, people drive instead of fly. Driving is far more dangerous. Why the switch?

buildup.text: The availability heuristic: we judge frequency by how easily examples come to mind.

discovery.text: Vivid, recent, or emotional events are easier to recall—so we overestimate how common they are.

twist.text: Shark attacks get news coverage. Falling coconuts don't. Coconuts kill more people every year.

climax.text: Doctors misdiagnose when a rare disease was in last week's journal. Recency warps clinical judgment.

punchline.text: Easy to recall doesn't mean likely to happen.

quiz.question: What drives the availability heuristic?
options: How easily examples come to mind
